faq.subtitle: Still deciding between splits or plans? Here is what most lifters ask first.

items.question: What is the difference between Upper/Lower and Push/Pull/Legs?
items.answer: Upper/Lower splits your week into two session types, hitting every muscle group twice if you train four days. Push/Pull/Legs separates pushing muscles, pulling muscles, and legs into three distinct sessions, which suits lifters training five to six days a week.

items.question: Can I switch between plans later?
items.answer: Yes. Membership and Coaching customers can switch their active split at any time from their dashboard, and One-Time customers can upgrade to Membership with credit applied toward their first month.

items.question: Do I need a full gym to follow these programs?
items.answer: Most programs are written for a standard gym with barbells, dumbbells, and basic machines. Each plan also includes simplified substitutions for home gyms with limited equipment.

items.question: Is coaching worth it if I am new to training?
items.answer: Coaching is especially useful early on, since your coach corrects form, adjusts load each week, and keeps your split realistic for your schedule and recovery.

items.question: Can I cancel my membership anytime?
items.answer: Yes, Membership and Coaching are both month-to-month with no contract. You can cancel from account settings and you will keep access until the end of your billing period.

story.title: From one whiteboard to a full training system
story.paragraph1: ShiftSplit was founded by strength coach Jordan Cole after years of watching lifters bounce between random programs, chasing soreness instead of progress. The first version was a laminated upper/lower split taped to a squat rack.
story.paragraph2: That rack-side experiment grew into a structured method for sequencing upper, lower, push, pull and leg days so volume, recovery and intensity actually line up with a lifter's week, not against it.

items.question: How is the upper/lower split structured?
items.answer: Each training week alternates two upper-body and two lower-body sessions, with an optional fifth conditioning day you can skip or swap for a full rest day.

items.question: Can I switch between upper/lower and full-body programming?
items.answer: Yes. Change your split from your account at any time and your next training block will be rebuilt around the new structure automatically.

items.question: Do I need a full gym to follow the programs?
items.answer: The default programming assumes a standard gym setup, but most lifts include a dumbbell-only or home-gym substitution so you're never stuck.

items.question: How fast will I hear back from support?
items.answer: Our coaching team answers every message within one business day, and usually much sooner on weekdays.

items.question: Is coaching feedback included with every plan?
items.answer: Form-check video reviews and weekly check-ins come with the Coached and Elite plans. The free split templates are self-guided.

faq.title: Before you pick a split
faq.subtitle: The questions lifters ask most before starting a new program.

items.question: How do I know which split is right for me?
items.answer: It comes down to how many days a week you can realistically train and your main goal. Fewer days usually points to full body or upper/lower, more days opens up push/pull/legs or a bro split.

items.question: Can I switch splits mid program?
items.answer: Yes. You can move between splits at any time and your logged history carries over, so you keep your progression data when you switch.

items.question: Do I need a full gym to follow these programs?
items.answer: No. Each program lists substitutions for home or limited equipment setups alongside the standard gym version of each exercise.

items.question: How long before I should expect progress?
items.answer: Most lifters see consistent load or rep progression within 6 to 8 weeks of following a program without missing sessions.

faq.title: Choosing the right program
faq.subtitle: The most common questions lifters ask before picking a split.

items.question: How do I choose between Upper/Lower, Push/Pull/Legs and Full Body?
items.answer: Start with how many days a week you can realistically train. Three days points to Full Body, four days to Upper/Lower, and five to six days opens up Push/Pull/Legs for higher training frequency.

items.question: What equipment do I actually need?
items.answer: Every split is built around a barbell, a rack, a bench and a set of dumbbells. Push/Pull/Legs also benefits from a cable machine, though each session lists a substitution if you train at home.

items.question: Can I switch programs once I've started?
items.answer: Yes. You can change your split at any time from your account dashboard and your next training block is rebuilt around the new schedule automatically.

items.question: Which program is best if I'm a complete beginner?
items.answer: Full Body is the easiest entry point since it repeats the same core lifts three times a week, building technique and consistency before moving to a higher-frequency split like Upper/Lower.
